text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is often called a "silent killer" because it typically causes no signs or symptoms. Most people with high blood pressure feel completely normal and do not realize their numbers are high.
You can check your current categories through the American Heart Association or learn more from the CDC High Blood Pressure Overview.
When Symptoms Do Appear (Dangerously High or Rising Blood Pressure)
While rare during normal hypertension, severely elevated blood pressure or a rapid spike can sometimes trigger physical signs:

list.snippet: Fatigue or feeling exhausted all the time
Vision changes (such as blurred vision or dark spots)
Blood spots in the eyes (broken tiny blood vessels)

text_blocks.snippet: If a blood pressure reading is higher than 180/120 mm Hg, wait one minute and re-test. If the second reading remains above 180/120 mm Hg and is accompanied by any of the following emergency symptoms, call 911 immediately:

list.snippet: Sudden weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking

text_blocks.snippet: (If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg but you do not have these symptoms, contact your doctor right away for guidance).
Because symptoms are rarely reliable, the only way to know if you have high blood pressure is to measure it regularly with a blood pressure cuff at a doctor’s office or at home.
